keyFindings.description: This round corrected the measured Go cache pair everywhere but left the number derived from the old pair unchanged, in five places. 'Six copies of identical content would be about 5.5 GB of a 20 GiB volume' sits two sentences from the measurement that disproves it: the pair is 751 MB + 375 MB = 1.126 GB, so six copies are about 6.8 GB and 5.5 GB is the five redundant copies that sharing avoids. Four of the five sites state it as the size of six with no qualifier — api/version.go:257 (the shipped contract-33 entry), docs/kubernetes.md:1800, manifest_test.go:659 and packages/pi-legion/CHANGELOG.md:90 (published). The fifth, manifest.go:790, ends 'spent on nothing', which makes it the saving and so defensible. This is the only quantitative justification for making the Go caches issue-shared, and it is wrong against the figure printed beside it; two of the four carrying sites are permanent published records. The fix is 'five redundant copies, about 5.6 GB' (or 'six copies, about 6.8 GB') in the four.

The concurrency proof reads as a self-contradiction this round's own push created. ':1801-1803 says the live proof was two `go build ./...` at once against one empty shared pair, both exit 0 in 227 s, 'filling 751 MB of build cache and 375 MB of module cache'; :1803-1806 then says 'What those figures measure, here and in the sizing above, is one build: a cold `cd packages/daemon && go build ./...` into an empty pair'. Both are true of the same run and the reconciliation is the point the paragraph is making — two concurrent builds of one module leave one build's worth of content in the shared pair, which is what makes sharing safe and cheap — but the paragraph never says it, so a reader meets 'two builds at once' and 'is one build' in adjacent clauses with nothing joining them. One clause fixes it.

The pull request body's `Why:` line still motivates the change with 'Go build cache 297 MB, Go module cache 192 MB' — the pair this round removed from the tree. The tester's closing check was scoped `grep -rn '297 MB|192 MB' docs/ packages/`, which cannot see the body. The body is what the merger quotes and what the next reader of this change meets first, so it should not carry the figure the change itself disproved by 2.5x. A body edit changes no commit, so this one costs nothing and voids nothing; `Size:` wants refreshing with it. (My own two lines, `Look at first` and `Not proven / risk`, I have already brought up to this head.)
